On Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 9:28 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> can you confirm whether the errors are predominantly decode/oom (5xx internal) or inference-time kernel failures?

Quick summary from runtime diagnostics (initial):
- We27re seeing an intermittent alignment mismatch between the new int8 kernel path and the KV cache when sequence padding occurs. That causes a small percentage of requests to hit a failure branch which surfaces as 5xx.
- The chronic p99 spike appears tied to a fallback path that calls into a slower float32 exec when the quantized path raises an alignment exception — adding ~60-120ms on those requests.
- Throughput drop is consistent with retries and backpressure when the error rate crosses ~0.8%.

Immediate recommendation: soft rollback (traffic split 90/10 back to v4.1) + disable the new alignment optimization flag while we push a patch. Patch ETA: 6-8 hours if we reproduce locally; hotfix ETA for a constrained rollout: 3-4 hours.

I27ll join the 10:00 PST bridge with a debug build and short repro.
-- Vivek

Subject: Re: Urgent: latency & 5xx surge after v4.2 quant profile

Roger / Lydia — follow-up and resolution summary (short):

- Root cause: an alignment-handling regression in the v4.2 int8 execution path that triggers a fallback to float exec for certain padded sequences. This produced intermittent 5xxs and elevated p99 latency under high concurrency.
- Remediation executed: we performed a soft rollback (90/10) on 2026-12-01 10:12 PST, disabled the alignment optimization flag, and deployed a targeted hotfix to the runtime. By 14:00 PST the 5xx rate had normalized to <0.2% and p99 returned to baseline.
- Customer impact: throughput dropped ~18% during the initial incident window; estimated affected requests: ~26k; we propose a 6% usage credit for the impacted period per our SLA/contract (see attached calc).
- Next steps: formal PSR attached, engineering change to add a pre-deploy alignment test in our CI for quant kernels, and a cross-team retro scheduled for 2026-12-07.

Attachments: PSR_SummitEdge_20261203.pdf, credit_calc_SE-4491.xlsx

Karthik Iyer
